+import typing
+
+from sqlalchemy.engine.row import Row
+
+from databases.interfaces import Record as RecordInterface
+
+
+class Record(RecordInterface):
+    """
+    A row wrapper providing both sequence (tuple-like) and mapping access.
+
+    SQLAlchemy 2.0's ``Row`` only supports positional access and attribute
+    access by column name; key-based access (``row["name"]``, ``dict(row)``)
+    has to go through ``Row._mapping``.  The ``Record`` interface exposed by
+    this library however promises key access, so we wrap the underlying
+    ``Row`` to restore that behaviour.
+    """
+
+    __slots__ = ("_row",)
+
+    def __init__(self, row: Row) -> None:
+        self._row = row
+
+    @property
+    def _mapping(self) -> typing.Mapping:
+        return self._row._mapping
+
+    def keys(self) -> typing.KeysView:
+        return self._row._mapping.keys()
+
+    def values(self) -> typing.ValuesView:
+        return self._row._mapping.values()
+
+    def __getitem__(self, key: typing.Any) -> typing.Any:
+        if isinstance(key, (int, slice)):
+            return self._row[key]
+        return self._row._mapping[key]
+
+    def __iter__(self) -> typing.Iterator:
+        return iter(self._row)
+
+    def __len__(self) -> int:
+        return len(self._row)
+
+    def __getattr__(self, name: str) -> typing.Any:
+        return getattr(self._row, name)
